title: Flood Safety & Evacuation Guide
summary: Floods can develop rapidly. Move to higher ground immediately, avoid floodwaters, and follow emergency evacuation orders.
precautions: Move to higher ground or upper floors immediately if water begins rising.
Turn off electrical main switches and gas valves before evacuating.
Do not walk, swim, or drive through moving floodwaters. Just 6 inches of moving water can knock you down.
Keep emergency supplies (food, clean water, flashlight, power bank, first aid kit) packed in a waterproof Go-Bag.
Listen to emergency broadcasts for official updates and evacuation routes.
evacuation: Follow designated evacuation routes provided by rescue authorities.
Avoid taking shortcuts through low-lying areas, underpasses, or near riverbanks.
Disconnect all electrical devices before leaving your premises.
Assist elderly neighbours, children, and individuals with disabilities.
Proceed directly to the nearest designated relief shelter or high-altitude safe zone.
firstAid: Treat hypothermia by removing wet clothing and wrapping the victim in dry blankets.
Clean and disinfect any open wounds exposed to floodwaters with clean water and antiseptic to prevent infection.
Perform CPR if victim is non-responsive and not breathing after submersion.
Do not ingest floodwater under any circumstances. Drink only sealed bottled or boiled water.
emergencyChecklist: Clean Drinking Water (at least 3 liters per person per day)
First Aid Kit & Essential Prescription Medicines
Fully charged Power Bank & Mobile Phone
Important personal documents stored in a sealed ziplock bag
dos: DO move immediately to higher ground.
DO stay tuned to official government emergency alerts.
DO boil or disinfect drinking water.
DO keep phone lines free for emergency calls.
donts: DON'T attempt to walk or drive through flooded roads.
DON'T touch fallen power lines or electrical equipment.
DON'T drink tap water or floodwater.
